comments.text: The processor port's direction register, $2F from the reset on: the game never writes it.

One step of the world, called once a pass in the race (and twice while the car is lowered at the start): the car's physics, the opponent, the wheels against the road, the forces and the moves. The step takes longer than a frame, so between its parts it calls FLIP_IF_READY, which finishes the switch to the newly drawn bitmap as soon as the interrupt has made it. The second half (springs, drag, torques) runs only once $C307 is set, when the car is on its wheels.

Where the car's three points of contact (the two front wheels and the back) sit from its middle, from the rotation matrix: the first two are row $22 (and row $23 for the other axis) less and plus half the sum of rows $1F and $1A (half the difference of rows $1C and $21), the third is row $22 (row $23) negated. Low bytes at $0130-$0132 and $0136-$0138, high bytes three on.

Moves the car by its velocity: each axis of the position ($0100-$0108, three bytes an axis) by a quarter of its velocity ($0109/$010F), upwards by a half; the height is kept below $03E8. Turns the three angles ($0121/$0124) by their speeds ($016A/$016D), keeping the pitch and the roll within the limits at $0A55 and $0A57 (the second pair, wider, while $C373 and $C359 say the car is coming down from a jump): one that hits its limit stops turning that way. Sets $C3DC bit 7 when the roll is past 15, and $33/$69 to $3C less the pitch over 32.
The highest pitch and roll MOVE_CAR allows ($2C), and the higher one while landing ($0A).
The lowest pitch and roll ($D3), and while landing ($F5).
Adds each of the three forces ($0115/$011B) to its axis of the velocity ($0109/$010F).
Adds each of the three torques ($0118/$011E) to its axis of the spin ($010C/$0112).

For each point of contact: its height above the road (the road's height at $C340/$C343/$C3CE less the car's at $C346/$C349/$C3D1, less $0E for the car's own height), kept at $0179/$017C/$C3D4; how far its spring is pressed ($0148/$014B, from the change in that height since the last step at $0142/$0145), 0 when it is off the road. A spring pressed past 4 that was below 2 counts a landing at $C3BC; past $C38B plus 7 the bump damages the car: the excess, half again, is added to the point's damage at $C3C3 (once a bump: $E1 counts its steps against $209B) and $C352 is set. Then the springs' mean ($0160/$0161), three times the front pair's difference at most 16 either way ($0166/$0167, the roll's force), and the front pair's mean less the back's ($014E/$014F, the pitch's); $6A is non-zero while any spring is pressed. With none pressed and the car not hanging from the crane, the pitch's force is held at a limit set by the pitch and the track. Then the car's grip on the track ($EC11, $2176) and, on a landing, sound effect 3.

The forces the road puts on the car through the springs: $015B (upwards, from $013D and $0171), $015C (sideways: the sideways speed $0150, worn down by $0159 while both are positive and held to what the road can take, plus $0172 and $013E), and the pull along the road (SIDE_GRIP).

The torques: about the first axis ($0118/$011E), the pitch's force ($014E) less a sixteenth of the spin, plus a quarter of the sideways force ($015C) while on the road; about the third ($011A/$0120), the roll's force ($0166) less a sixteenth of the spin.

The force along the road ($015A/$015D): the spring's ($013C plus $0170) less the speed along it ($0154/$0157), held to what the road can take (ROAD_HOLD); $C3C6 is set to $80 when it was held, as the wheels slide.
How hard the road can push, in $14/$15: twice the spring's force $0171/$0174 while any spring is pressed and that force is positive, else 0.

Takes a share of the velocity from the forces, $C350 parts in 256 shifted right by 2, 4 or 6 places. On the road the share is the largest of the three speeds along the road ($0154-$0159), less 20 while the boost ($C308) is on with the engine running ($C36A); otherwise $C0: a fixed share shifted 2 places when the car is skidding sideways ($E4 past 2) or wrecked ($6B), 4 places when it hangs from the crane or $0E is set.

Divides the three points' heights by 8; from their differences, the sines of the car's pitch ($0178, with bit 7 flipped) and roll ($0176), and their cosines through COSINE_OF; then the springs' mean force along each axis of the car ($0170-$0175), by those sines and cosines.
The size of the signed sixteen bits in A and $14, as a byte ($FF from 256 up), in $56, and from the table at $B080 the cosine of an angle with that sine, in $57.

Once a pass of the race: runs down $82, the passes left of showing the last lap's time, and puts the best lap back when it ends; moves both cars' lap clocks on by a pass and checks each for a lap (LAP_CHECK); checks for the race's end (LAPS_DONE); and runs the countdown at $6C (twice a pass while $C373 bit 7 is set).

Runs the countdown at $6C, while it is from 1 to $7F: down by one each pass the car is off the road or hanging from the crane, or while it is 6 or more. Bit 2 of it goes to $C399, for a flashing lamp. When it reaches 0 it becomes $80 and $C351 is set.
Compares lap clock X with clock Y, minutes ($8398), seconds ($82B0) and hundredths ($8298), all in decimal: when X's time is the shorter it is copied over Y's, and the carry comes back clear.
Sets the lamp for the best lap and draws the best lap's time (clock 2) in the dashboard's fourth place, with its hundredths. X is kept.

Counts a lap for car X (0 the player, 1 the opponent): when its piece ($C374) is the one the start line is on ($C77C), and $C376 bit 7 is clear (cleared once the car has passed piece $C767, half way round), $C378 goes up by one and $C376 bit 7 is set. For the player the lap number is drawn, and from the second lap on the lap's time shows for 25 passes. A lap faster than the best becomes the best (FASTER), and when it was the opponent's it shows with its lamp. Then the car's lap clock starts again from 0.

Ends the race when either car has run its laps ($C378 equal to $C354) and it has not ended ($C364): the countdown starts at $2C if none is running, and a message shows: RACE LOST when the lamp says the opponent finished first (and $C362 is set to $80), RACE WON in a league race, LAPS OVER in practice. Then copies $C395 into bit 6 of $C362.
Prints $1F, X and Y: moves the printer's column to X and its row to Y.
Draws the player's clock (0) in the dashboard's third place, with its hundredths only while $82 says a lap's time is showing. X is kept.
Prints the digit in A (adds $30, '0').
Sets clock X to 0:00.00.
Moves clock X on by 0.14 seconds, the length of a pass of the race (seven frames of the 50 a second): the race is timed by its passes, not by the clock on the wall.

Adds A hundredths to clock X in decimal mode; past 59 seconds the minutes go up, to 9 at most. The player's clock is drawn each time it carries into the seconds, unless a lap's time is showing or no lap has started.

After a bump ($C352): the crack across the top of the frame is drawn to the mean of the three points' damage ($C3CB, from $C3C3-$C3C5, with $1B88). A bump of 20 or more ($C35C) also takes one from $C719, a count the player keeps from race to race (10 at the start of a season), drawn with $F021 and $F673 for 64 passes ($C302, then $F668), with sound effect 1; a smaller bump makes sound effect 4.
The best lap's lamp: colour 11 while the best is the opponent's ($C395), 7 otherwise.
Sets the colour RAM of the lamp at $DBDA-$DBDB to Y.
The lamp for who leads: colour 11 when $F5E9 comes back with N clear, which LAPS_DONE takes as the opponent ahead, 7 otherwise; Y comes back with it.
Sets the colour RAM of the lamp at $DBCC-$DBCD to Y.

Every fourth pass: the sixteen bits at $39/$3A times 5/16, drawn as four digits (thousands, hundreds, tens and units) into the dashboard's sprites, after a blank, or a minus while $C36A bit 7 is set. Taking 100 off with a borrow from the high byte takes 101 by mistake, as the carry is clear there.
The speed bar's length from the speed along the road ($0159): twice its excess over 17, plus one, times $B7/256, drawn with command $43; 0 below 17 or from $91.

Draws clock Y in place X of the dashboard (the sprite rows at $1296) as M:SS.HH: the minutes, the colon, the seconds, the point and the hundredths, which are blank unless A has bit 7 set. $6F records which sprites changed.
Where each of the dashboard's four times starts in the sprite data from $4000.
Draws the L (laps) and the B on the dashboard.

Puts a message into the two sprites at $7F80 and $7FC0, from the table at $1329: Y is its first byte and A its number of groups, each a place in the sprites and three characters. A '<' moves the whole line half a character (four pixels) left. The glyphs' rows 1-6 are taken from the font. $C355 says a message is up. X is kept.
The table offset of the message showing.
Its number of groups.

The cockpit messages: WRECK, RACE WON, RACE LOST, DROP START, PRESS FIRE, PAUSED, LAPS OVER, DEFINE KEYS, STEER LEFT, STEER RIGHT, AHEAD +BOOST, BACK +BOOST, BACK, VERIFY KEYS, FAULT FOUND; each in groups of a sprite offset and three characters.
The two dots between minutes and seconds: bit 7 set in the bytes 6 and 15 before X, rows 1 and 4 of the time.
Draws digit A into the sprite bytes from X, a pixel to the left. These four entries share the code at $1430: each takes rows 1-6 of the glyph and goes down a sprite row (three bytes) for each.
Draws digit A from X two pixels to the right, the two that spill into the next byte, which is overwritten.
Draws digit A from X a pixel to the right, keeping each byte's bit 7.
Draws digit A into the sprite bytes from X as it is. A digit $F0 draws a space and $FD a minus.
Points $1E at the glyph of character A plus $30 (its low seven bits) in the font at $7FC0, eight bytes a character, and sets Y to 1.
Places, points and colours sprites 2-7 for the dashboard (the clocks, the messages and the front wheels), with the sprites' shared colours black and white, and turns them on ($6E keeps which are on).
Sprites 2-7's pointers.
Sprites 2-7's colours.
Sprites 2-7's x positions; the table runs into the next.
Sprites 2-7's y positions.

Moves the two front wheels' sprites up and down with the first two points' springs ($83/$86), through the sine table at $A700, from the height $1C; a wheel that would sit too low has its sprite turned off and its top drawn into the bitmap (command $40) instead, and one coming back up has the bitmap's drawing put back to its rest.
Draws a wheel's top at height A (command $40).
The car is wrecked: unless the countdown is running it drops ($0E = 2, $1C = $92, $3C = $82), the countdown starts at $3C and WRECK shows.

While $C9 is set: a swerve of sixteen passes ($C30F) steers by the wave at $1601 ($C30D one way, $C30E the other, $C357 the throttle). A new one starts at random, the more often the higher $C773, when $C353 allows it and $0710 for piece $C375 does not forbid it.
Sixteen steps of a wave, signed, for SWERVE.
Clears the league's points ($C728-$C763) and $C77F, puts the twelve drivers back in order at $C758 and sets each one's count at $83B0 back to 10.
Keeps the random numbers' state ($02-$06) at $1648.
Sets the random numbers' state ($02-$06) from the five bytes ending at $1643 plus Y: Y = 4 the fixed seed at $1643, Y = 9 those SAVE_RANDOM kept.
The random numbers' first state, which LOAD_RANDOM puts at $02-$06 with Y = 4.
Where SAVE_RANDOM keeps the state.

Starts a frame's view: each column's top and bottom limits ($C640/$C680) from those kept at $C280/$C2C0, the edges at $0280/$02C0 cleared, the view cleared with the bonnet put back (CMD_CLEAR_VIEW), $F1DC, and the flags $C3A9, $C3DA, $6D and $C303 cleared.

Draws a frame's view of the track. From the piece the car is over ($FF6A, or $F117 from $AF and $B1, into $2E and $C374) it draws that piece and the ones ahead, each with DRAW_PIECE, POINTS_TO_LINES and NEXT_PIECE: the first two, then two more, or five more while the car is lowered at the start ($2F), or on Draw Bridge (track 5) up to two more as the car nears piece $31. When no piece is under the car it is off the track and wrecked ($6B = $C0). In a league race the opponent moves (OPPONENT_MOVE) and its car is placed among the pieces. Then the view's column limits, the fills, and the sky above the track (CMD_FILL_ABOVE).

Draws piece $2E: its place and shape ($F02F, $F0C5, PIECE_POINTS), then which way it is seen ($C3A8: bit 7 when it is behind the eye, bit 6 when seen from its far end); each of its points, near to far or far to near as it is seen, is turned into the eye's frame ($A026), projected (PROJECT_X, PROJECT_Y) and checked against the last point on its side (OVERLAP); points before $27 are left out. Last, every point in sight is turned by the roll ($280E).

Point X against the last point drawn on its side of the road ($CC for the left, $CD for the right): when it lies further out across the screen, the road's edge folds back over itself there, so the point is marked ($A350 = 2) and a copy of it made (point X plus $20, at $A220/$A2B8), projected and turned, to close the edge.

The last two points of the piece just drawn become the first two of the next (all six of their tables), and $CC/$CD start again from them; after a piece behind the eye ($C3A9) the next starts from scratch ($D0 = 0).

Puts the piece's points into the tables, in pairs across the road, from its shape's two lists ($98 for the left edge, $CA for the right): a point's height is in the high three bits of its byte (shifted left once) and its distance along in the low four, or in two bytes each when $A2 bit 7 is set; each is added to the piece's place ($3F/$35, $40/$36) into $8040 and $A330. Points past the distance $19 (from $2A less $D3, how far the view reaches) are left out ($A330 = $80). $8080 records the start line's piece ($C766) and the points whose first byte has bit 7 set, which get a line across the road.

Joins the piece's points with lines, pair by pair: each point to the last one on its side of the road (ALONG_SIDE) and to its copy where the edge folds back (TO_COPY), the near or far line first as the car is rolled ($C3DC, $0126). The colour of each side alternates by pair ($FC01, from $C6 and $D8), the same from the 40th pair on; a pair marked at $8080 gets a line across the road, striped on the start line ($CF73). The opponent's car is drawn when its pair is reached ($E195, $E1B1).
The line from point $C6 to the last point drawn on its side ($CC or $CD, as $A0 says), by $FE91.
The line from point $C6 to its copy, point $C6 plus $20, by $FE91.

Each of the first two points of the piece that lies inside the view's columns but in front of the screen ($A2E4, $A24C) is moved along its edge towards the point before it ($8D, from $E808 and $E631), so that the line to it can be drawn; then re-projected ($E641).

Grows the crack across the top of the windscreen to match the damage: while its length $25 is below $C3CB, one more pixel pair. Each step wanders up or down a row at random (rows 3-5 of the bitmap's top line, kept at $1C15) and cuts a notch three rows deep into the frame at $6026. A step into a gap already open adds one to the damage instead (SET_DAMAGE). When the crack reaches the far side ($78), or the damage reaches $80, the car is wrecked.
Sets each point's damage ($C3C3-$C3C5) to twice the mean ($C3CB).
The row the crack is on (3 to 5).
The masks that keep the other three pixel pairs of a byte.
The masks of the four pixel pairs of a byte.
Runs command $3F, the crane's chains.
Clears the menus' panel in the bitmap at $4000: sixteen character rows of 28 characters from $4B60.
Sets up the screen for a race: eight rows filled (command $55), $3A3C, and the dashboard unpacked (command $32).

Reads the joystick ($F79E, into $66: bit 0 forward, 1 back, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire). Left and right steer ($C5 = $F1 or $0F) while a spring is pressed. Fire is the boost ($C398 is 0 while it is held). Forward drives ($0150/$0151 from $C384/$C385) and the engine keeps driving after it is let go ($C39B bit 7); back brakes ($0150/$0151 = $FF10) and stops the drive. No drive while the car is lowered or dropped, or past $78 along the road. Then $F60F.

With $C359 set, in place of the view's column limits: a line across the whole view (points 2 and 3, from -376 to 632) at the horizon's height for the pitch ($33/$69), in colour $2C, then back to $3D. $C365 keeps the roll's sign ($0124) meanwhile.
Runs command $3C, the moving bridge, on Draw Bridge (track 5) only.

Where across the road the opponent aims ($2C, from its place $B0; the player's is $2B). Close behind the player ($39/$3A, the distance between the cars, and less than $32 apart across) it may bump ($209C, OPP_BUMP); within $18 it goes round (LINE_ROUND), unless its driver's flags at $AEE0 (bit 3) say to keep its line; nearer than $32 it holds the player's line (bit 1, LINE_HOLD) or passes (LINE_PASS), as it does within $C8 for a driver with bit 5, and always once it is ahead ($C36A bit 7). Otherwise its own line: $40 or $6E across (bit 3), mirrored for the odd-numbered drivers ($C773), or the middle when either of the next two pieces says so ($B240). Then it steers towards that line by ten a pass ($C357 can push it either way) while a wheel is on the road ($C9), keeping between $20 and $E0. $C308 is set while the cars are within $40 and either the opponent is ahead or they are in line; then the car in front has less drag.
Aims $20 or $E0 across, away from the side the player is on ($77), when the cars are within $38 across.
Aims $20 or $E0 across, to pass the player on the side with more room, when the cars are within $38 across.
Aims at the player's line ($2B).
The first piece, from the player's ($C374) on round the track, whose number at $044E is X; $FF when there is none. X is kept.
Where PIECE_FROM_HERE keeps X.

Moves the opponent's car, while it races ($C37C): its piece's place ($F02F), its wheels (OPP_WHEELS), a swerve now and then (SWERVE), its engine and grip (OPP_ENGINE, OPP_GRIP) and its speed (OPP_SPEED); then along the road by its speed ($D6/$D7) times $BD, in $A1/$23/$C4, on to the next piece ($C375) as $C4 passes the piece's length $BE.
Lowers the opponent's car onto the track ($E4DA) from a height above the road of $68 to $E7, at random, for each of its wheels.

Picks the opponent's limits for the race at random, from ranges for its track (the second set while $C71A is set): the top speed at $2099 ($BFAA/$BFB2), $209A ($BFBA/$BFC2) and $209B ($C774 or $C775). It runs RANDOM 256 times first. Nothing while $31A1 and $C77F are both set.

The opponent's speed $D6/$D7: plus the engine's push ($C3B6/$C3B7, less its speed again and $23 more on a climb, $B2), less a drag of its speed squared over 64 (its speed taken 20 lower while it is in front and close, $C308), plus, while a wheel is on the road, the slope's pull from the heights of its front and back wheels ($07EC-$07F2); never below 0.
The tail of OPP_SPEED: A:$14 added to the speed $D6/$D7.
The opponent's engine: $C3B6/$C3B7 from $C386/$C387, 25 less during a swerve ($C30F), none while no wheel is on the road ($C9).

The piece's speed limit ($0710, or the opponent's own at $2099 when that is lower and the piece's has no bit 7) against the opponent's speed $D7: over it, the engine's push is reversed ($C3C7 set); far over it, or under it, the push is doubled, except just under a limit it has reached.
The opponent's top speed for the race, from OPP_PICK.
A second limit for the race, from OPP_PICK.
A third, from OPP_PICK, which WHEELS_ON_ROAD counts a bump's steps against.

The cars meet: while the opponent races and is in the air or the player's springs are free, and its back wheel is within $C0 of the player's height ($46/$64, plus $28), three times ($C369) it pushes the player's car up ($0180/$0183); close beside it pushes sideways ($0182); and along by the difference of their speeds ($0181/$0184), once a bump ($E0). The pushes' size, plus 2, is added to each point's damage ($C3C3-$C3C5) and $C352 is set.

Takes in a bump's pushes ($C371): the opponent's speed less the push along (never below 0), its wheels' speeds less the push up over 16, the player's springs' forces ($0170-$0175) plus the pushes, which are then cleared; sound effect 2.

The opponent's three wheels as springs: each one's height ($07CC/$07D0) against the road's under it ($07EC/$07F0) and the spring's length ($28, or $7C on a piece with $B2 bit 7), at most $60 below; the spring's push ($07C4/$07C8, up to $3FF), and $C9 non-zero while any wheel is on the road. Each wheel's speed ($07E4/$07E8) is a share of the three pushes and its own, over 8. A driver with bit 2 of its flags now and then (one pass in 16) bounces its back wheel ($07DE = $A0) when all are nearly still. The speeds are added into the heights (half of them), the wheels kept together (OPP_SPREAD), and the opponent's model's points placed ($8040/$A330, points $3C-$3F).
Which of the model's points ($3C-$3F) each wheel sets.
The difference of the heights of wheels X and Y: its size in A:$14, its sign in bit 7 of $17.

Keeps wheels X and Y within A:$51 of each other in height: the higher is lowered to it and their speeds averaged (all three's when Y is 2). With Y = 2 and no wheel on the road, when wheel X rises no faster than the back wheel by $10, the car is tilted: the front wheels' speeds up by 4 and the back's down by 4.
The tilt OPP_SPREAD gives the three wheels' speeds, low bytes.
High bytes.
Sets the speeds of wheels X and Y ($07DC/$07E0) both to their mean.

Point X's place across the screen ($A200/$A298) from its distance across ($78:$52) and its depth ($77:$51), through PROJECT_LOG; a point on the left (a negative distance) is moved two pixels further out. While the menus draw the track's picture ($F3C1) the game rewrites these first three bytes to a JMP to PROJECT_X_PAIR.
PROJECT_X with the distance's low byte in A.

Divides by logarithms. The distance across, made eight bits with a count of the shifts it took, gives its logarithm ($AA00 low, $AB00 high, plus $A610 for the shifts) in $70/$71; the depth's the same way in $A9/$AA. Their difference, turned back by EXP, is the point's offset from the middle of the screen ($A7/$A8, or $32/$3E on the other side), into $A200/$A298 for point $16. $AB/$AC keep the depth's logarithm less the result's, plus $20, for PROJECT_Y. The branch at $24F8 is rewritten by PROJECT_X ($90, BCC, or $B0, BCS) to swap the sides for a negative distance.

Point X's height on the screen ($A24C/$A2E4): its height ($8040/$A330) less the eye's ($37/$38), by its logarithm less $AB/$AC, turned back by EXP, from the horizon's line ($33/$69). The 8 taken off the logarithm is the operand at $262B, which the menus' picture of the track sets to $0B.

The antilogarithm of A:$14 (from $E0:00 up; below that it gives $FF for 0 and 0 for anything else): its top bits pick an entry in the tables at $A800, $A880 and $A900, and the fractions at $AC00, $AC80 and $AD00 decide the rounding.

When the roll ($0126, with the top two bits of $0123) has changed: its sine and cosine from the quarter-wave table at $A700. $0300-$037F become the running sums of the sine (the high byte of $80 plus n times it), $0380-$03FF those of twice the cosine; $C328/$C334 half of $0100 plus n times the sine, and $C310/$C31C n times the cosine, for n from 1 to 8. The loops rewrite their own operands ($277B, $2781, $27A6, $27AD, $27B8, $27BE).
The roll the tables were last built for.
Its top two low bits.
Turns point X on the screen by the roll, about the middle ($80, $80), unless it is out of sight ($A330 bit 7).
Turns point X by the roll. A point near the middle (both high bytes 0) is turned with the tables of running sums at $0280-$03FF alone, when that does not overflow; any other by ROLL_FAR.
Turns point X by the roll with the products of its distances from the middle and the roll's sine and cosine: the whole eighths from $C310-$C33F and the rest from $0300-$03FF.

The game's random numbers: moves the forty-bit shift register at $02-$06 on by eight bits, mixing its fourth and fifth bytes back in, and gives its new first byte in A ($53 and $54 are its scratch). X and Y are kept.

Draws a piece of the wreck, X the speck, at column $80A0 and row $C260 of speck $C6: lines joined end to end ($FEC9), their steps from the tables at $2A3E (across) and $2A4D (down), ten lines for an odd X and five for an even one; bit 1 of X picks the colour ($FC01).
Where each shape's steps start in the tables.
Each shape's number of lines, less one.
Each shape's first column, added to the speck's.
The lines' steps across.
The lines' steps down.

Where a piece of the wreck, X, starts: the first column out from the middle ($40), right then left, where the outline of the view's top ($C640) steps by 4 or more, a few pixels about it at random. $C260 = $D2 (none) when there is no such column.

Saves or loads a file through the KERNAL: a save while $C77B is set, a load otherwise. After the menus' messages ($3848, $3884, $95E2) and the file's name ($A1CB, $EDAB, $9448), with the KERNAL banked in: the screen at $0400 filled with spaces, the KERNAL set up again (IOINIT, RAMTAS, VECTOR from $0800, CINT), the disk's old file scratched (command $47), and the file saved or loaded (SETLFS on device 1 or 8 by $0840, SETNAM, SAVE or LOAD): the 192 bytes from $8000 under the twelve-letter name at $AEC1, or while $C367 is set the bytes from $4000 to $40FF or $41FF under the one-letter name at $94D6. A failure (READST, or the disk's answer to command $47) sets $C301 bit 7, and $C39A then. The random numbers ($02-$06) are kept around it (SAVE_RANDOM, LOAD_RANDOM), as RAMTAS clears the zero page.
The device for each answer to "disk or tape" ($0840): 1, the tape, or 8, the disk.
Runs command $45, the view cleared, with $3DF8 as its flags.
Runs command $3E, the fill above the edges.
Runs command $46, the view's colour RAM brought up to date.
Runs command $41.
Runs command $42, while $6D bit 7 says there are spans to fill.
Runs command $3D, the view's column limits, or HORIZON while $C359 is set.
Sixteen pieces fly while the car is wrecked, with a stones' sound of $0A and the car's speed ($0188), 16 at most.
All 32 specks of dust gone ($C260 = $D4).

The dust thrown up from the road while the car is on it ($C30A, or lowered at the start, $0E), not wrecked and moving ($0188): 32 specks, with the sound of the stones (sound effect 1, its pitch at $AF8C from the speed, 50 at most, or now and then 3 or $0D).

With A the sound's pitch less 2 and X the last speck. In the air ($6A 0) all go (DUST_CLEAR). On the road each speck is rubbed out where it was and moved (DUST_PLOT): it falls faster by 2 a pass ($4120) and moves across by $4100. One that has gone below the view starts again at random on the road's edge ($C280; for a wreck, DEBRIS_START), going up by a quarter of $C350 and a little more, and out from the middle by an eighth of its distance from it.

Draws speck X: two pixels, one above the other, cleared with the masks at $A4C0, at its column ($80A0) and row ($C260); for a wreck, a piece of debris (DEBRIS). A speck outside the view (rows $41 to $B7, columns below $80) is gone ($D2), and Z clear says so.
Points $1E at the byte of the bitmap being drawn ($12) that holds pixel column X of row Y, less Y, and reads it.

The size of the speed along the road ($0159/$0156) into $0188, and the engine's note from it ($5D, which the interrupt adds into $5F each frame, clicking the engine at each carry): eight times the speed below 8, twice it plus $30 from there, $FF at most. In the air the note falls by a quarter each pass.

The turn on the car. Its heading against the road's under it: the piece's direction ($0189/$018A, flipped by $A4) less the car's ($0122/$0125), with a quarter turn either way on a piece with $B2 bit 7 ($2EFD/$2F00); its size in $7F:$7D. Steering ($C5) turns the car by the speed along the road ($0159) times $C8 (more, or less, on such a piece, by the side of its turn, $9D), plus the difference over 16 when it steers towards the road's direction. Without steering the car is turned towards the road's direction, by the difference times the speed plus 10, over 128, at least 1. More than $1E off, it is turned back at once by the excess. The turning force $0119/$011F is the steering's less the car's spin about that axis ($010D/$0113), 0 in the air ($6A). The next piece is taken when the car is within 2 of the piece's end ($BE, $C3).
The quarter turns STEERING adds on a piece with $B2 bit 7, low bytes.
High bytes.

Draws the windscreen's frame into the bitmap at $4000 from the picture at $6000: the edges above and below the view (patterns of 24 bytes repeated across, from $6130, $6270, $63B0 and $64F0), the two pillars (FRAME_PILLAR), and the corners.
A pillar of the frame: eighteen character rows of 16 bytes into the bitmap from ($1E), A its high byte, from the three rows at X:Y and below in turn, then the corners' bytes.

Asks the interrupt to show the bitmap just drawn: flips $C306, sets $12 to the bitmap to draw into next ($20 for the one at $6000, or $18 plus the $E8 at $A1F2, which comes to 0, for the one at $4000) and $C370 to match ($80 or 0), and sets $C37A for the interrupt, with interrupts off while it does.
Finishes a flip the interrupt has made ($C37B set), through FLIP_DONE; otherwise nothing.
Once the interrupt shows the new bitmap: the view's colour RAM brought up to date for it (command $46), two dashboard colours set, and $C37A and $C37B cleared.
Turns multicolour on ($D016 bit 4) and shows the bitmap at $6000 with the screen at $5C00 ($D018 = $78), through SET_VIDEO.
Turns multicolour off and shows the bitmap at $4000 with the screen at $7C00 ($D018 = $F0), through SET_VIDEO.
With interrupts off, keeps A in $FA and writes it to $D018, selects video bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) through CIA 2's port A, and makes the background black.

Sets up the screen the menus are drawn on: multicolour, the bitmap at $4000 with the screen at $7C00 (through SET_VIDEO, interrupts off while CIA 2 and $D018 change), the screen at $5C00 filled with X ORed with $0E, and the bitmap cleared by COPY_VIEW_OR_CLEAR.
The screen colours MENU_SCREEN was given in X.
Fills the screen at $5C00-$5FFF with A.

With A of 2 or more, copies the bitmap at $6140-$77BF to $4140-$57BF, a page at a time from the top: the picture built in one bitmap is shown in the other. With A below 2, fills 20 rows of the bitmap at $4000 with $AA and the five rows from $5900 with 0.
Non-zero while PRINT_CHAR_RAW is taking the column and the row after a $1F.
How many bytes of the $1F sequence PRINT_CHAR_RAW has taken.
Prints the character in A with PRINT_CHAR_RAW, keeping A, X and Y. Every piece of text the game shows in its bitmaps goes through here.

Prints the character in A into the bitmap at $4000, seven pixels wide, at column $85C5 (of 45) and row $85C6. $1F takes the next two bytes as the column and the row; 9 moves one column on; $7F moves back one and rubs out the character there; codes from $80 do nothing. The glyph is eight bytes at $7FC0 plus eight times the code. Its seven-pixel column is turned into a byte and a shift, and the glyph is shifted across the two bytes it straddles, kept from the pixels on either side by masks. With bit 7 of $85D0 set the character is drawn half a row lower, as the menus' highlighted lines are. The column moves on, back to 0 after 44.
The column PRINT_CHAR_RAW prints at, in seven-pixel steps (0-44).
The character row PRINT_CHAR_RAW prints at.
Where PRINT_CHAR keeps A.
Where PRINT_CHAR and WAIT_KEY keep X.
Where PRINT_CHAR and WAIT_KEY keep Y.
The mask that keeps the pixels to the left of the glyph in its first byte.
The mask that keeps the pixels to the right of the glyph in its second byte.
The glyph's first byte column (eight pixels each).
How many pixels the glyph is shifted right within its first byte.
$40 while neither shift key is held, so WAIT_KEY reads the second half of its table.
The number of the last key WAIT_KEY returned: it waits for this key to be let go first.
Bit 7 set (command $20) draws the characters half a row lower.
Bit 7 set while PRINT_CHAR_RAW rubs out a character with $7F.

Tests one key, X its number in the keyboard matrix: bits 0-2 pick the line it drives low on CIA 1's port A ($DC00), bits 3-5 the bit it reads back on port B ($DC01). Gives X = $FF with N set when the key is held, X = 0 with Z set when not.
The eight single bits KEY_SCAN drives and reads, bit 0 to bit 7.

Waits for the last key it returned to be let go, then for any key, and gives that key's character in A from the table at $9125: the first half when a shift key is held, the second when not. The two shift keys themselves are skipped. X and Y are kept.

Starts a sound effect from the seven bytes at X (low) and Y (high): the slot (which voice), the control byte (its waveform), attack and decay, sustain and release, the pitch's high byte, the pulse width's high nibble, and how long the gate is held, in frames. The voice is silenced, set up and gated on; EFFECT_TICK lets it go.
The pulse width byte of the last effect started.
The slot of the last effect started.
Frames each slot's gate is still held; bit 7 set while it is being started.
Each slot's pitch, high byte.
Each slot's release time in frames, from its release nibble.
Frames left of each slot's release, before it is silenced.
Each slot's control byte with the gate bit cleared, written to let it go.
The SID register offset of each slot's voice: 0, 7 and 14.
The release times, in frames, for the sixteen values of the release nibble; roughly the SID's own release lengths, frame by frame.
Called by the interrupt every frame for slot 1, the second voice: counts down the frames its gate is held, then lets the gate go, then after its release time cuts the voice with CUT_EFFECT.
Stops the effect in slot X (command $15): its count is cleared and its voice's control and sustain-release registers set to 0.

The command dispatcher: A is the command, X (and Y) its argument. $01 shows the bitmap at $4000 in hi-res and $02 the one at $6000 in multicolour ($FE keeps which), $03 sets up the menus' screen, $10 copies or clears the view, $20 sets the half-row flag, $81 tests a key, $15 stops an effect, $32 unpacks the dashboard, $55 fills rows, $34 saves or restores what a menu covers, and $3C-$47 run the race's jobs: the drawbridge, the view's fills, the crane's chains, the front wheels, the speed bar, the opponent's table, the view cleared, the row colours and the disk's commands. Any other command does nothing.

Puts the dashboard together from the table the start-up left under the I/O area at $D400: thirteen runs of bytes, each with its length and its destination in the first 39 bytes, copied into the bitmap; then 320 bytes for the screen at $7C00 and the 320 colour bytes, which go to colour RAM; and seventeen rows from $4A00 cleared. Interrupts from the video chip are off while the RAM under the I/O is in.

With X below $80, saves the part of the bitmap at $62A0 that a menu covers in the race (eight rows of 256 bytes and a ninth of 64) to $57C0, and colour RAM to $6DE0. With X from $80, puts both back, and copies the tables under the I/O area at $D000-$D3FF and $DD00-$DDFF to $7C00 and $7B00.
Fills $52 rows of 320 bytes, from the address in X (low) and Y (high), with A.

The Draw Bridge's moving ends (command $3C, called on track 5 only). A count of passes at $C300 rises and falls over 32 passes; it rewrites the points of object $5F, the bridge's two ends, so that they rise and fall, and their heights at $0740-$0744. While either car is on pieces $33-$37, next to the bridge, it stays down ($E7 = 12).
Half the count in A picks a step from $8A0F; $0740, $0741 and $0742 become $C6 plus one, two and three steps.
The steps BRIDGE_HEIGHTS adds, for the sixteen positions of the bridge.
The heights $0743 and $0744 take, for the sixteen positions of the count.

Command $3D: for each of the view's 64 columns, keeps the lowest the top limit ($C680) and the bottom limit ($C640) have been: a height (256 less the sixteen bits at $69 and $33, 255 when those are 0 or less, 0 when they are past 256) less and plus that column's slope at $0380, mirrored when $0126 is negative.

Command $3E: in each of the view's 32 character columns (pixel columns $40-$BF, four to a byte), from the lowest of its four edges at $C600 upwards, each pixel above its own edge is set to colour 2. Once a row has all four, the rest of that character row is filled whole, and the character row is kept at $01C1 plus X (7 when the column never got that far), for SET_ROW_COLOURS.

Command $3F: the two chains the car hangs from before the start, drawn from row $C36B up to the top of the view at pixel columns $54 and $A8. While $2F is 0 their ends rise by a step that grows by 8 a pass ($C36C), until row $5F.
Draws one chain at pixel column X, upwards from row $C36B: links eight rows tall and two bytes wide, odd and even links taken in turn from the masks at $8BCD-$8C0C.
The masks that keep the background around a chain's links, left byte, for the sixteen rows of two links.
The masks that keep the background around a chain's links, right byte.
The chain's pixels, left byte, sixteen rows.
The chain's pixels, right byte.

Command $40: draws the top of a front wheel, X 0 the left and 1 the right, at the height in $14: eight rows taken from the tables at $8C70 (left) or $8C94 (right), starting further into them the lower the wheel, into both bitmaps. The wheels bounce with the suspension.
The left front wheel's top, three columns of bytes ($8C70, $8C78 and $8C80) read upwards from an offset set by the wheel's height.
The right front wheel's top, three columns of bytes ($8C94, $8C9C and $8CA4).

Command $41: counts the pixel columns from $60 to $61, kept inside the view ($40-$BF) and widened to whole characters ($41 to $55), once more each at $0240. A column counted for the first time has $C500 set to $C0 and starts at $C1. When $60 is past $61 nothing is counted and bit 7 of $6D and of $C303 is cleared.

Command $42: in each character column from $41 to $55, fills the pixels between the edges at $0240 and those at $C600 with colour 2, by parity: TOGGLE_EDGES flips each pixel's bit in the row flags at $C400 at both its edges, and going up the column a pixel is filled while its bit is set. Bit 7 of a row's flags marks the top row of a character row. The flags are flipped back afterwards.
For the four pixel columns from X, each whose edge at $0240 is above its edge at $C600 flips its bit (8, 4, 2 or 1) in the row flags just above the first edge and at the second.
For each set of the four pixels in a byte (bit 3 the leftmost), the mask that turns those pixels from colour 3 to colour 2.

Command $43: the bar above the speedometer's scale (row 21 of the dashboard, from column 12, two pixel rows deep), X/2 pixels long (less 64 from 64 on). Only what changed since the last length ($C34F) is drawn: whole bytes of four pixels and one part byte at the end.
The bar's last byte with one, two and three of its four pixels lit.
A byte of the bar with all four pixels lit.
A byte of the bar with none lit.

Command $44: a value for each of the track's pieces at $0710, from the last piece back to the first. A piece listed at $075E takes its own from $0769, and when that has bit 7 set the three pieces before it get bit 7 too. A piece whose kind (the low four bits at $0400) has bit 7 set at $B240 takes X. Any other takes the value of the piece after it plus 10, up to $7F, carried in $14 (from $7C).
The X PIECE_TABLE was given.
The X CLEAR_VIEW was given: bit 7 draws the bonnet into the bitmap at $4000 too.

Command $45: fills the view in the bitmap being drawn ($12: 0 for $4000) with colour 3, thirteen character rows of 32 characters from $62A0 (or $42A0), and puts back the bonnet below it from its copy at $C000-$C25F; into the bitmap at $4000 only when bit 7 of X is set.

Command $46: for each of the view's 32 character columns whose top character row of colour 2 has moved since the last frame ($0200 was, $0201 now, four bytes a column), sets the screen bytes of the rows between: to $C76B for the rows it rose past, to $0E for those it fell back from. The rows' addresses come from the tables at $A400 (low) and $A418 (high).

Command $47, with the KERNAL in: nothing unless $0840 says there is a drive. X = 0 sends the drive "I0" (initialise); any other X sends "S0:" and the name at $AEC1 (scratch: the old file goes before a save), when $C77B says there is one. Comes back with carry set on an error; "file not found" (4) is not one.
"S0:" and the twelve characters of the file's name, the command DISK_COMMAND sends to scratch a file.
The name, copied from $AEC1.
"I0", the command that initialises the drive.
The character for each of the 64 keys, by key number (the bit read on port B times 8 plus the bit driven on port A): the first 64 with a shift key held, the next 64 without.
Scratch for MUL_S8_U8's negated product.
Scratch for MUL_S16_MATRIX: the matrix entry's high byte, its sign.
The sign byte SHIFT16 shifts in from the top: $00 or $FF.
Where SIN_COS keeps X while it works.
Multiplies A by $15, both unsigned, by shift and add: the product's high byte comes back in A and its low byte in $14. The carry always comes back clear. Every multiply in the game goes through here.
Tests one key: X is its number in the keyboard matrix (row times 8 plus column). Asks the command dispatcher (command $81) to scan that key and gives back Z set when it is held. Y is kept.

The sine and cosine of the angle in A (high) and $14 (low), a whole turn being $10000. Rounds the angle to the table's 512 steps (adds $0020), then reads the quarter-wave table at $A700 twice, once forward and once mirrored, to give the two signed results in $56 and $57. $58 keeps the rounded angle's high byte and $59 two bits that tell the callers which quadrant it is in, so they can set the signs. X is kept.
Multiplies the signed byte in A by the magnitude in $15, whose sign is bit 7 of $5A: the signed 16-bit product comes back in A (high) and $14 (low).
Clears the sign in $5A and runs on into MUL_S16_S8: the signed 16-bit number in A:$14 times the positive factor in $15, divided by 256.

Multiplies the signed 16-bit number in A (high) and $14 by the factor in $15, whose sign is bit 7 of $5A, and keeps the top two bytes of the product: A:$14 times $15 over 256, signed. $5A comes back holding the product's sign.

Multiplies the signed 16-bit number in A:$14 by entry X of the car's rotation matrix (the two bytes at $0774,X and $079C,X, of which it uses a quarter, eight bits, as the factor) and divides by 256. The result in A:$14 is signed. This is how the physics turns a vector from one frame of reference to the other, one term at a time.
The tail the signed multiplies share: $16 and $14 hold the magnitude, $15 the factor and A the sign byte; works out both partial products, adds them and applies the sign.
Negates the two-byte number in A (high) and $14 when the N flag is set on entry, so a caller can test a sign (a BIT or a load) and call this straight after. With N clear it returns at once.
Negates the two-byte number in A (high) and $14, two's complement. $15 is left holding the high byte it was given.

Turns the signed 16-bit value in A:$14 back into an angle by table: it takes the top bits as an index into the steps at $AD00 (the extra precision) and $A700 (the quarter-wave table) and draws a straight line between two neighbouring steps with the remaining bits. Bit 6 of the input picks which end of the table it counts from, and bit 7 the result's sign. Comes back in A:$14.
Entry X of the rotation matrix ($0774,X and $079C,X) times 5/16, as a half plus an eighth, halved, and negated when $5A is negative. Comes back in A:$14.
Squares the signed 16-bit number in A (high) and Y (low) into the four bytes $16-$19, by three 8-bit multiplies.

Shifts the signed number in A (high) and $14 by Y bits: right for Y from 1 to $7F, the sign coming in from the top, and left for Y from $80 up (by 256 minus Y), the bits that leave the top collecting in $2D. Y = 0 leaves it alone. The sign it shifts in runs out after eight places, so a negative number shifted further right picks up zeros.
Adds the two-byte number in $19:$18 to A (high) and $14, leaving the sum in A:$14 and the carry. $15 is left holding the A it was given.
Moves $2E, the piece being drawn, on to the next round the track ($C764 pieces), into X too.
Moves $2E back to the piece before.

What PROJECT_X runs while the game has rewritten its first bytes to a JMP here (for the track's picture in the menus, $F3C1): the depth ($77:$51) halved, and the distance across ($78:$52) halved and moved $30 on, projected twice (F42D), the first result's logarithm kept in $AB/$AC.
Puts A in $15 and runs on into LOAD_14. Callers use it to start a two-byte sum: the high byte goes to $15, the low comes back in A with the carry clear.
Loads $14 into A and clears the carry.
